Subject: CCPA addendum — telemetry tagging and subprocessor evidence

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Legal has a couple of follow-ups on the US state addendum (CCPA/CPRA) before we can finish procurement:

1) Telemetry tagging: we need a brief explanation of how telemetry that contains customer identifiers is tagged/flagged in Redwood’s pipeline so it can be excluded from sale/exchange workflows. A simple mapping is fine — which fields are candidate identifiers, where they land, and who has access.

2) Subprocessor evidence: as part of our SOC2 review we need recent evidence that the subprocessors handling telemetry (edge caches, analytics) are contractually bound under the same ‘service provider’ obligations. A one-page summary or a redacted contract extract would work.

3) Onshore fallback: we have a clause requiring an onshore fallback for certain categories of telemetry in the event of cross-border restrictions. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports an onshore fallback and the expected lead time to activate it?

Can you loop in whoever owns the DPA/subprocessor list? We’d like to keep this short — ideally 48–72 hours to move to signature.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Liu
Director of Privacy — HealthCorp

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and attached a telemetry mapping workbook plus a preliminary subprocessor evidence summary.

1) Telemetry tagging: see tab "telemetry_map" in the attached redwood-telemetry-map.xlsx. High level: any identifier fields (email, user_id, device_id) are tagged at ingress by the routing layer; tags are propagated through the KV cache and telemetry pipeline so they can be filtered before batch exports or analytics. Access controls restrict raw identifier access to the storage/ops role; aggregated metrics are available to analytics.

2) Subprocessor evidence: attached subprocessor_evidence_summary.pdf contains redacted SOW lines and contract stamping that show the SP-class obligations for our edge cache provider and analytics vendor. If you need named copies we can provide further redaction.

3) Onshore fallback: we support an onshore fallback for telemetry categories A/B (PII-linked telemetry) by routing to regionally provisioned GPU pools and onshore S3 storage. Activation path is documented — typically 5–10 business days to provision and validate depending on committed capacity; faster with a Dedicated contract.

Marissa — can you review the redlines in ccpa-addendum-redlines.docx and advise if legal wants tighter language on "processing purpose" vs. "use restrictions"? Aditya — can you confirm SLA/lead times for a standard onshore fallback activation?

Dana — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Thanks Mina. Quick note from legal side:

- The customer requested that the service provider definition explicitly prohibit any resale or "monetization" of customer telemetry. We already have Seller/Resale carve-outs in place for hosted customers, but I propose tightening the addendum language to explicitly call out telemetry categories and sale definition.

- I'd like to replace the current catch-all "for the provision of services" language with three enumerated processing purposes (model serving, caching & ops, telemetry/analytics) and then attach the telemetry_map as an exhibit. This creates a clear bright-line for HealthCorp to prove the telemetry that is excluded from "sale".

- For subprocessor evidence, the summary Mina provided is good; legal would like a single redacted appendix that includes the contract clause number and signature block for each subprocessor handling telemetry. If HealthCorp needs named artifacts, we can request permission from the subprocessors to produce a redacted extract.

Mina, can you draft the revised clause text and I’ll drop it into the docx and return for countersign? I’ll also add a short acceptance checklist for HealthCorp’s procurement team.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

On the fallback timing: ADITYA — please add the standard provisioning steps and the expected time to enable onshore fallback for a non-dedicated tenant (estimate in business days).
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Dana Liu <privacy@healthcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CCPA addendum — telemetry tagging and subprocessor evidence

Hi all — operational estimate below for the onshore fallback activation for telemetry categories A/B:

- Step 1: Provision onshore storage and GPU pool (network + IAM config) — 1–3 business days (if capacity available).
- Step 2: Route toggle and validate ingress tagging rules in staging — 1 business day.
- Step 3: Run end-to-end throughput and encryption validation, plus sampling to ensure tags are excluded from downstream exports — 1–3 business days.
- Step 4: Customer acceptance checklist and go-live — 1 business day.

Total typical time: 4–8 business days. For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity we can usually do this in 1–3 business days as parts are pre-provisioned.

Note: if there are subcontractor approvals required (some subprocessors are global), we may need a brief legal sign-off window to confirm contract alignment. We recommend contracting a 10-business-day SLA for activation in procurement if HealthCorp needs a guaranteed timeline.

-Aditya
Director, Runtime Operations
Redwood Inference
